NKJV.1: Now it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to make war against it, but could not prevail against it.
NKJV.2: And it was told to the house of David, saying, “Syria’s forces are deployed in Ephraim.” So his heart and the heart of his people were moved as the trees of the woods are moved with the wind.
NKJV.3: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, “Go out now to meet Ahaz, you and Shear-Jashub your son, at the end of the aqueduct from the upper pool, on the highway to the Fuller’s Field,
NKJV.4: and say to him: ‘Take heed, and be quiet; do not fear or be fainthearted for these two stubs of smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and the son of Remaliah.
NKJV.5: Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah have plotted evil against you, saying,
NKJV.6: “Let us go up against Judah and trouble it, and let us make a gap in its wall for ourselves, and set a king over them, the son of Tabel”—
NKJV.7: thus says the Lord GOD:  “It shall not stand, Nor shall it come to pass.
NKJV.8: For the head of Syria is Damascus, And the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be broken, So that it will not be a people.
NKJV.9: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, And the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If you will not believe, Surely you shall not be established.” ’ ”
NKJV.10: Moreover the LORD spoke again to Ahaz, saying,
NKJV.11: “Ask a sign for yourself from the LORD your God; ask it either in the depth or in the height above.”
NKJV.12: But Ahaz said, “I will not ask, nor will I test the LORD!”
NKJV.13: Then he said, “Hear now, O house of David! Is it a small thing for you to weary men, but will you weary my God also?
NKJV.14: Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a Son, and shall call His name Immanuel.
NKJV.15: Curds and honey He shall eat, that He may know to refuse the evil and choose the good.
NKJV.16: For before the Child shall know to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land that you dread will be forsaken by both her kings.
NKJV.17: The LORD will bring the king of Assyria upon you and your people and your father’s house—days that have not come since the day that Ephraim departed from Judah.”
NKJV.18: And it shall come to pass in that day That the LORD will whistle for the fly That is in the farthest part of the rivers of Egypt, And for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
NKJV.19: They will come, and all of them will rest In the desolate valleys and in the clefts of the rocks, And on all thorns and in all pastures.
NKJV.20: In the same day the Lord will shave with a hired razor, With those from beyond the River, with the king of Assyria, The head and the hair of the legs, And will also remove the beard.
NKJV.21: It shall be in that day That a man will keep alive a young cow and two sheep;
NKJV.22: So it shall be, from the abundance of milk they give, That he will eat curds; For curds and honey everyone will eat who is left in the land.
NKJV.23: It shall happen in that day, That wherever there could be a thousand vines Worth a thousand shekels of silver, It will be for briers and thorns.
NKJV.24: With arrows and bows men will come there, Because all the land will become briers and thorns.
NKJV.25: And to any hill which could be dug with the hoe, You will not go there for fear of briers and thorns; But it will become a range for oxen And a place for sheep to roam.

NASB.1: Now it came about in the days of Ahaz, the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin the king of Aram and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to [wage] war against it, but could not conquer it.
NASB.2: When it was reported to the house of David, saying, 'The Arameans have camped in Ephraim,' his heart and the hearts of his people shook as the trees of the forest shake with the wind.
NASB.3: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, 'Go out now to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-jashub, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the fuller's field,
NASB.4: and say to him, 'Take care and be calm, have no fear and do not be fainthearted because of these two stubs of smoldering firebrands, on account of the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.
NASB.5: 'Because Aram, [with] Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has planned evil against you, saying,
NASB.6: 'Let us go up against Judah and terrorize it, and make for ourselves a breach in its walls and set up the son of Tabeel as king in the midst of it,'
NASB.7: thus says the Lord GOD: 'It shall not stand nor shall it come to pass.
NASB.8: 'For the head of Aram is Damascus and the head of Damascus is Rezin (now within another 65 years Ephraim will be shattered, [so that it is] no longer a people),
NASB.9: and the head of Ephraim is Samaria and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you will not believe, you surely shall not last.'''
NASB.10: Then the LORD spoke again to Ahaz, saying,
NASB.11: 'Ask a sign for yourself from the LORD your God; make [it] deep as Sheol or high as heaven.'
NASB.12: But Ahaz said, 'I will not ask, nor will I test the LORD!'
NASB.13: Then he said, 'Listen now, O house of David! Is it too slight a thing for you to try the patience of men, that you will try the patience of my God as well?
NASB.14: 'Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Behold, a virgin will be with child and bear a son, and she will call His name Immanuel.
NASB.15: 'He will eat curds and honey at the time He knows [enough] to refuse evil and choose good.
NASB.16: 'For before the boy will know [enough] to refuse evil and choose good, the land whose two kings you dread will be forsaken.
NASB.17: 'The LORD will bring on you, on your people, and on your father's house such days as have never come since the day that Ephraim separated from Judah, the king of Assyria.'
NASB.18: In that day the LORD will whistle for the fly that is in the remotest part of the rivers of Egypt and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
NASB.19: They will all come and settle on the steep ravines, on the ledges of the cliffs, on all the thorn bushes and on all the watering places.
NASB.20: In that day the Lord will shave with a razor, hired from regions beyond the Euphrates ([that is], with the king of Assyria), the head and the hair of the legs; and it will also remove the beard.
NASB.21: Now in that day a man may keep alive a heifer and a pair of sheep;
NASB.22: and because of the abundance of the milk produced he will eat curds, for everyone that is left within the land will eat curds and honey.
NASB.23: And it will come about in that day, that every place where there used to be a thousand vines, [valued] at a thousand [shekels] of silver, will become briars and thorns.
NASB.24: [People] will come there with bows and arrows because all the land will be briars and thorns.
NASB.25: As for all the hills which used to be cultivated with the hoe, you will not go there for fear of briars and thorns; but they will become a place for pasturing oxen and for sheep to trample.

ESV.1: In the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah the king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to wage war against it, but could not yet mount an attack against it.
ESV.2: When the house of David was told, “Syria is in league with  Ephraim,” the heart of Ahaz  and the heart of his people shook as the trees of the forest shake before the wind.
ESV.3: And the LORD said to Isaiah, “Go out to meet Ahaz, you and Shear-jashub  your son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool on the highway to the Washer's Field.
ESV.4: And say to him, ‘Be careful, be quiet, do not fear, and do not let your heart be faint because of these two smoldering stumps of firebrands, at the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria and the son of Remaliah.
ESV.5: Because Syria, with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has devised evil against you, saying,
ESV.6: “Let us go up against Judah and terrify it, and let us conquer it  for ourselves, and set up the son of Tabeel as king in the midst of it,”
ESV.7: thus says the Lord GOD: “‘It shall not stand, and it shall not come to pass.
ESV.8: For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. And within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered from being a people.
ESV.9: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you  are not firm in faith, you will not be firm at all.’”
ESV.10: Again the LORD spoke to Ahaz:
ESV.11: “Ask a sign of the LORD your  God; let it be deep as Sheol or high as heaven.”
ESV.12: But Ahaz said, “I will not ask, and I will not put the LORD to the test.”
ESV.13: And he  said, “Hear then, O house of David! Is it too little for you to weary men, that you weary my God also?
ESV.14: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
ESV.15: He shall eat curds and honey when he knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good.
ESV.16: For before the boy knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land whose two kings you dread will be deserted.
ESV.17: The LORD will bring upon you and upon your people and upon your father's house such days as have not come since the day that Ephraim departed from Judah — the king of Assyria!”
ESV.18: In that day the LORD will whistle for the fly that is at the end of the streams of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
ESV.19: And they will all come and settle in the steep ravines, and in the clefts of the rocks, and on all the thornbushes, and on all the pastures.
ESV.20: In that day the Lord will shave with a razor that is hired beyond the River  — with the king of Assyria — the head and the hair of the feet, and it will sweep away the beard also.
ESV.21: In that day a man will keep alive a young cow and two sheep,
ESV.22: and because of the abundance of milk that they give, he will eat curds, for everyone who is left in the land will eat curds and honey.
ESV.23: In that day every place where there used to be a thousand vines, worth a thousand shekels  of silver, will become briers and thorns.
ESV.24: With bow and arrows a man will come there, for all the land will be briers and thorns.
ESV.25: And as for all the hills that used to be hoed with a hoe, you will not come there for fear of briers and thorns, but they will become a place where cattle are let loose and where sheep tread.

CSB17.1: This took place during the reign of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah king of Judah: <sup>ⓙ</sup> Aram’s King Rezin and Israel’s King Pekah son of Remaliah went to fight against Jerusalem, <sup>ⓚ</sup> but they were not able to conquer it.
CSB17.2: When it became known to the house of David <sup>ⓛ</sup> that Aram had occupied Ephraim, <sup>ⓜ</sup> the heart of Ahaz <sup>[1]</sup> and the hearts of his people trembled like trees of a forest shaking in the wind.
CSB17.3: The LORD said to Isaiah, “Go out with your son Shear-jashub <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓝ</sup> to meet Ahaz at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, <sup>ⓐ</sup> by the road to the Launderer’s Field.
CSB17.4: Say to him: Calm down and be quiet. Don’t be afraid or cowardly <sup>ⓑ</sup> because of these two smoldering sticks, the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram, and the son of Remaliah.
CSB17.5: For Aram, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted harm against you. They say,
CSB17.6: ‘Let us go up against Judah, terrorize it, and conquer it for ourselves. Then we can install Tabeel’s son as king in it.’”
CSB17.7: This is what the Lord GOD says: It will not happen; it will not occur. ⓒ
CSB17.8:
The [3] chief city of Aram is Damascus,
the chief of Damascus is Rezin
(within sixty-five years
Ephraim will be too shattered to be a people),
CSB17.9:
the chief city of Ephraim is Samaria,
and the chief of Samaria is the son of Remaliah.
If you do not stand firm in your faith,
then you will not stand at all.
CSB17.10: Then the LORD spoke again to Ahaz:
CSB17.11: “Ask for a sign <sup>ⓓ</sup> from the LORD your God — it can be as deep as Sheol or as high as heaven.”
CSB17.12: But Ahaz replied, “I will not ask. I will not test the LORD.”
CSB17.13: Isaiah <sup>ⓔ</sup> said, “Listen, house of David! Is it not enough for you to try the patience of men? Will you also try the patience of my God? <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.14: Therefore, the Lord himself will give you <sup>[4]</sup> a sign: See, the virgin will conceive, <sup>[5]</sup> have a son, and name him Immanuel. <sup>[6]</sup> <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.15: By the time he learns to reject what is bad and choose what is good, <sup>ⓗ</sup> he will be eating curds <sup>[7]</sup> and honey. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.16: For before the boy knows to reject what is bad and choose what is good, the land of the two kings you dread will be abandoned.
CSB17.17: The LORD will bring on you, your people, and your father’s house such a time as has never been since Ephraim separated from Judah: <sup>ⓙ</sup> He will bring the king of Assyria.” <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.18:
On that day ⓛ
the LORD will whistle ⓜ to flies
at the farthest streams of the Nile
and to bees in the land of Assyria.
CSB17.19:
All of them will come and settle
in the steep ravines, in the clefts of the rocks, ⓝ
in all the thornbushes, and in all the water holes.
CSB17.20: On that day the Lord will use a razor <sup>ⓐ</sup> hired from beyond the Euphrates River — the king of Assyria <sup>ⓑ</sup>  — to shave the hair on your heads, the hair on your legs, and even your beards.
CSB17.21:
On that day
a man will raise a young cow and two sheep,
CSB17.22:
and from the abundant milk they give
he will eat curds,
for every survivor in the land will eat curds and honey. ⓒ
CSB17.23:
And on that day
every place where there were a thousand vines,
worth a thousand pieces of silver,
will become thorns and briers. ⓓ
CSB17.24:
A man will go there with bow and arrows
because the whole land will be thorns and briers.
CSB17.25:
You will not go to all the hills
that were once tilled with a hoe,
for fear of the thorns and briers.
Those hills will be places for oxen to graze
and for sheep to trample.

WEB.1: In the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.
WEB.2: David’s house was told, “Syria is allied with Ephraim.” His heart trembled, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the forest tremble with the wind.
WEB.3: Then Yahweh said to Isaiah, “Go out now to meet Ahaz, you, and Shearjashub your son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway of the fuller’s field.
WEB.4: Tell him, ‘Be careful, and keep calm. Don’t be afraid, neither let your heart be faint because of these two tails of smoking torches, for the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.
WEB.5: Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have plotted evil against you, saying,
WEB.6: “Let’s go up against Judah, and tear it apart, and let’s divide it among ourselves, and set up a king within it, even the son of Tabeel.”
WEB.7: This is what the Lord Yahweh says: “It shall not stand, neither shall it happen.”
WEB.8: For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within sixty-five years Ephraim shall be broken in pieces, so that it shall not be a people;
WEB.9: and the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If you will not believe, surely you shall not be established.’”
WEB.10: Yahweh spoke again to Ahaz, saying,
WEB.11: “Ask a sign of Yahweh your God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above.”
WEB.12: But Ahaz said, “I will not ask, neither will I tempt Yahweh.”
WEB.13: He said, “Listen now, house of David. Is it not enough for you to try the patience of men, that you will try the patience of my God also?
WEB.14: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
WEB.15: He shall eat butter and honey when he knows to refuse the evil, and choose the good.
WEB.16: For before the child knows to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land whose two kings you abhor shall be forsaken.
WEB.17: Yahweh will bring on you, on your people, and on your father’s house, days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah; even the king of Assyria.
WEB.18: It will happen in that day that Yahweh will whistle for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
WEB.19: They shall come, and shall all rest in the desolate valleys, in the clefts of the rocks, on all thorn hedges, and on all pastures.
WEB.20: In that day the Lord will shave with a razor that is hired in the parts beyond the River, even with the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet; and it shall also consume the beard.

WEB.22: and it shall happen, that because of the abundance of milk which they shall give he shall eat butter: for everyone will eat butter and honey that is left within the land.
WEB.23: It will happen in that day that every place where there were a thousand vines at a thousand silver shekels,  shall be for briers and thorns.
WEB.24: People will go there with arrows and with bow, because all the land will be briers and thorns.

NLT.1: When Ahaz, son of Jotham and grandson of Uzziah, was king of Judah, King Rezin of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah, the king of Israel, set out to attack Jerusalem. However, they were unable to carry out their plan.
NLT.2: The news had come to the royal court of Judah: “Syria is allied with Israel against us!” So the hearts of the king and his people trembled with fear, like trees shaking in a storm.
NLT.3: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, “Take your son Shear-jashub and go out to meet King Ahaz. You will find him at the end of the aqueduct that feeds water into the upper pool, near the road leading to the field where cloth is washed.
NLT.4: Tell him to stop worrying. Tell him he doesn’t need to fear the fierce anger of those two burned-out embers, King Rezin of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah.
NLT.5: Yes, the kings of Syria and Israel are plotting against him, saying,
NLT.6: ‘We will attack Judah and capture it for ourselves. Then we will install the son of Tabeel as Judah’s king.’
NLT.7:
But this is what the Sovereign LORD says: “This invasion will never happen;
it will never take place;
NLT.8:
for Syria is no stronger than its capital, Damascus,
and Damascus is no stronger than its king, Rezin.
As for Israel, within sixty-five years
it will be crushed and completely destroyed.
NLT.9:
Israel is no stronger than its capital, Samaria,
and Samaria is no stronger than its king, Pekah son of Remaliah.
Unless your faith is firm,
I cannot make you stand firm.”
NLT.10: Later, the LORD sent this message to King Ahaz:
NLT.11: “Ask the LORD your God for a sign of confirmation, Ahaz. Make it as difficult as you want — as high as heaven or as deep as the place of the dead. ”
NLT.12: But the king refused. “No,” he said, “I will not test the LORD like that.”
NLT.13: Then Isaiah said, “Listen well, you royal family of David! Isn’t it enough to exhaust human patience? Must you exhaust the patience of my God as well?
NLT.14: All right then, the Lord himself will give you the sign. Look! The virgin will conceive a child! She will give birth to a son and will call him Immanuel (which means ‘God is with us’).
NLT.15: By the time this child is old enough to choose what is right and reject what is wrong, he will be eating yogurt and honey.
NLT.16: For before the child is that old, the lands of the two kings you fear so much will both be deserted.
NLT.17: “Then the LORD will bring things on you, your nation, and your family unlike anything since Israel broke away from Judah. He will bring the king of Assyria upon you!”
NLT.18: In that day the LORD will whistle for the army of southern Egypt and for the army of Assyria. They will swarm around you like flies and bees.
NLT.19: They will come in vast hordes and settle in the fertile areas and also in the desolate valleys, caves, and thorny places.
NLT.20: In that day the Lord will hire a “razor” from beyond the Euphrates River — the king of Assyria — and use it to shave off everything: your land, your crops, and your people.
NLT.21: In that day a farmer will be fortunate to have a cow and two sheep or goats left.
NLT.22: Nevertheless, there will be enough milk for everyone because so few people will be left in the land. They will eat their fill of yogurt and honey.
NLT.23: In that day the lush vineyards, now worth 1,000 pieces of silver, will become patches of briers and thorns.
NLT.24: The entire land will become a vast expanse of briers and thorns, a hunting ground overrun by wildlife.
NLT.25: No one will go to the fertile hillsides where the gardens once grew, for briers and thorns will cover them. Cattle, sheep, and goats will graze there.

AMP.1: Now it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin king of Aram (Syria) and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to wage war against it, but they could not conquer it.
AMP.2: When the house of David (Judah) was told, "Aram is allied with Ephraim (Israel)," the hearts of Ahaz and his people trembled as the trees of the forest tremble in the wind.
AMP.3: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out to meet Ahaz [king of Judah], you and your son Shear-jashub, at the end of the aqueduct of the Upper Pool, on the highway to the Fuller's Field;
AMP.4: and say to him, 'Take care and be calm, do not fear and be weak-hearted because of these two stumps of smoldering logs, on account of the fierce anger of [King] Rezin and Aram and of the son of Remaliah (Pekah, usurper of the throne of Israel).
AMP.5: Because Aram, along with Ephraim (Israel) and the son of Remaliah, have planned evil against you (Judah), saying,
AMP.6: "Let us go up against Judah and terrorize it; and let us breach its wall and tear it apart [each of us taking a portion] and set up the son of Tabeel over it as its [puppet] king,"
AMP.7: for this is what the Lord GOD says, "It shall not stand nor shall it happen.
AMP.8: For the head (capital) of Aram is Damascus and the head of Damascus is [King] Rezin (now within sixty-five years Ephraim will be broken to pieces and will no longer be a people).
AMP.9: And the head (capital) of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah's son [King Pekah]. If you will not believe [and trust in God and His message], be assured that you will not be established."'"
AMP.10: Then the LORD spoke again to [King] Ahaz, saying,
AMP.11: "Ask a sign for yourself from the LORD your God [one that will convince you that God has spoken and will keep His word]; make your request as deep as Sheol or as high as heaven."
AMP.12: But Ahaz said, " I will not ask, nor will I test the LORD!"
AMP.13: Then Isaiah said, "Hear then, O house of David! Is it too small a thing for you to try the patience of men, but will you try the patience of my God as well?
AMP.14: Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Listen carefully, the virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and she will call his name Immanuel (God with us).
AMP.15: He will eat curds and honey when he knows enough to refuse evil and choose good.
AMP.16: For before the child will know enough to refuse evil and choose good, the land (Canaan) whose two kings you dread will be deserted [both Ephraim and Aram].
AMP.17: The LORD will bring on you, on your people, and on your father's house such days as have not come since the day that Ephraim (the ten northern tribes) separated from Judah—[He will call for] the king of Assyria."
AMP.18: In that day the LORD will whistle for the fly that is in the mouth of the rivers and canals of Egypt and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
AMP.19: These [armies, like flies and bees] will all come and settle on the steep and rugged ravines and in the clefts of the rocks, and on all the thorn bushes and in all the watering places.
AMP.20: In that day [when foreign armies swarm the land] the Lord will shave with a razor, hired from the regions beyond the Euphrates (that is, with the king of Assyria), [that razor will shave] the head and the hair of the legs; and it will also remove the beard [leaving Judah stripped, shamed and scorned].
AMP.21: Now in that day [because of the poverty caused by the invaders] a man will keep alive only a young milk cow and two sheep;
AMP.22: and because of the abundance of milk produced he will eat curds, for everyone that is left in the land will eat [only] curds and [wild] honey.
AMP.23: And it will come to pass in that day, in every place where there used to be a thousand vines, worth a thousand silver shekels, there will be briars and thorns.
AMP.24: People will come there [to hunt] with arrows and with bows because all the land will be briars and thorns.
AMP.25: As for all the hills which used to be cultivated with the pick and the hoe, you will no longer go there for fear of briars and thorns; but they will become a place where oxen are pastured and where sheep tread.

MSG.1: During the time that Ahaz son of Jothan, son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, King Rezin of Aram and King Pekah son of Remaliah of Israel attacked Jerusalem, but the attack sputtered out.

MSG.8:

MSG.9:

and the king of Samaria is the mere son of Remaliah.

you won't have a leg to stand on."

MSG.14: So the Master is going to give you a sign anyway. Watch for this: A girl who is presently a virgin will get pregnant. She'll bear a son and name him Immanuel (God-With-Us).
